data.narrative:
Vermeer, a Series A defense & security company founded by Brian Streem, is evaluated against a comp universe of 10 private and 2 public peers including Stark Defence, Singularity, and NODA AI at the same stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's $10M in total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $20M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—produces a median of $400M, with a range of $125M to $4.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in stage-equivalent valuations within defense & security.

Triangulating both methods yields a low of $17M, median of $210M, and high of $460M. The median estimate of $210M reflects approximately 21x the capital raised and sits at the geometric midpoint between the stage-progression floor and peer median. Key uncertainties include whether Vermeer's technology, market position, and fundraising trajectory more closely align with the lower-valuation peers (NODA AI) or the outlier (Stark Defence), and whether the peer set adequately represents Vermeer's competitive position within defense & security. The wide high-end range suggests caution around outlier comp valuations.
